content.text:
This figure is from AC 43.13-1B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Inspection and Repair, chapter 7 (aircraft hardware, control cables, and turnbuckles).
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure shows Table 7-12 (continued), a two-column table listing aircraft bolt part numbers, line drawings of each bolt, and descriptions of head style, material, thread type, strength, and temperature rating.

Left column:
- NAS1223-1235: Bolt, self-locking, hex. head 250 °F
- NAS1236: Bolt, universal, Tube-end, flaresless

- NAS1253-1260: Bolt, 100° head, flush hd., .0312 O.S. hi-torque
- NAS1261-1270: Bolt, hex. head, short thread
- NAS1271-1280: Bolt, 12 point hd., external wrenching
- NAS1297: Bolt, shoulder, hex. head
- NAS1303-1320: Bolt, hex. head, close tolerance, 160,000 psi
- NAS1414-1422: Lock bolt, shear 100° head, all. steel
- NAS1424-1432: Lock bolt, shear protruding head, steel
- NAS1503-1510: Bolt, 100° flush head, hi-torq.

Right column:
